package.description: Froststrap is a fork of Bloxstrap and Fishstrap, focused on performance and customization.

en-US.description: Froststrap is a fork of Bloxstrap and Fishstrap, focused on performance and customization.
en-US.name: Froststrap
en-US.releaseNotes:
Froststrap v2.0.7 - What's new?
The 2.0.6 cycle was a big internal change and with pressing for release, a few bugs slipped through the cracks.

Fixed
- Linux Sober logs not being found
  - whilst refactoring to fix logs being found and windows and macos, linux wasn't kept in mind, because sober doesn't use the same log file name pattern as the other clients
- Close To Desktop not actually closing Roblox (#279, @System_Error06)
- Potential dataloss via Windows installer
  - Settings were stored in same location as the installation, causing installer software in cases to wipe out everything not recognized by it
  - Settings and storage now live outside the install directory (inside %APPDATA%\Froststrap), so now theres clear seperation between your data and ours
- FFlagHandleAltEnterFullscreenManually was being reset to False on every load (#278, @Chipislol)
- Settings window asking about unsaved changes nobody made, and the close button doing nothing on a fresh install (#270, @Chipislol)
- NativeAOT publish failing on platforms running .NET 10.0.15 (#277, @Chipislol)
- Better path validation for themes

Removed
- Bootstrapper theme editor
  - After a vote in our Discord, 93% voted in favor of the removal
  - Instead the edit button will kick you to a instance of the current known editors (request for more) Zed, VSCode, and Sublime Text
  - Removes one of the maintenance burdens which we have

Changed
- CardExpander now animates when opening and closing
- Internal codebase restructure: Core and Localisation split into their own projects
  - We are researching into setting up the project for incremental builds
- Prepping for tech upgrade to .NET 11- all LINQ performance and other compiler warnings cleaned up
- Linux CI build job fixed where package installation could fail (#282, @Chipislol)
